feat(eval): an evaluator that can actually fail -- FAIL_TO_PASS / PASS_TO_PASS

THE GAP IT FILLS. `eval/harness.py:183` is `_recall`, i.e. `m not in
slice_text`: substring containment in a context slice. An honest RETRIEVAL
metric that never looks at a patch. This repo therefore had no correctness
evaluator at all, which is why the gate's rejection rate against the day's three
known-bad changes was 0 of 3.

MEASURED, ON THE REAL CORPUS, and this is the whole argument:

  candidate                       correctness evaluator   the repo's pytest_gate
  no-op (a comment)               not_fixed, 0/2          --
  PLAUSIBLE WRONG FIX             not_fixed, 1/2 green    exit 0 -- PASS, 19 passed
  correct fix + sabotage          regressed, 3 P2P broken --

A wrong-but-plausible patch passes the existing gate and is caught here. Also
driven through a real TaskAttempt with `gate=correctness_gate(...)` and NO spine
edit: right fix -> clean/fixed, wrong fix -> gates_failed/not_fixed.

FIVE OUTCOMES, with precedence could_not_run > regressed > not_fixed > fixed.
`regressed` outranking `fixed` is the distinction a boolean destroys: a patch
that fixes the bug AND breaks the regression set is reported as breaking it.

BOTH REVIEWER CORRECTIONS ARE IN. Invalidation is symmetric -- a PASS_TO_PASS
test failing on base is as fatal as a FAIL_TO_PASS test passing on it. And the
selection is FROZEN before the worktree exists: node-id lists, resolved base
sha, overlay revision and gate config, digested and recorded, with the task dict
never consulted again afterwards. There is no glob anywhere in the module, so a
test file a candidate adds cannot enter the set.

THE CORPUS SURVIVAL NUMBER IS THE MEASUREMENT, not a step toward it:
3 of 4 commits admitted, 22 of 41 candidate nodes. The losses are the report.

  * efd0ed6 SHIPPED NO TEST AT ALL -- a real fix with nothing that can witness
    it. Refused and reported, not invented around.
  * one node is xfail-marked: red before AND after the reference fix.
  * 19 nodes came back `missing` in the first pass because the deriver emitted
    unqualified names for unittest class methods. The before-state check
    refuted every one of them -- the anti-vacuity rule catching the tool that
    implements it.
  * a test the fix commit ADDED already passed on base, so it was demoted to
    the regression set rather than counted as a fix witness.
  * pytest's "not found" and "found no collectors for" are different facts, and
    conflating them invalidated 13 of 14 nodes of a real candidate.

`test_overlay` was not obvious and is essential: the base revision predates the
fix, so it also predates the fix's TESTS, and without overlaying them every
FAIL_TO_PASS node reads `missing`.

HOW THIS RELATES TO MUTATION SCORING -- neither subsumes the other, and the
honest version matters because promotion will eventually rest on it. Mutation
scoring grades the GATE (would it notice *a* bad change). FAIL_TO_PASS grades
the CHANGE (did *this* one fix *that* bug without breaking the regression set).
Mutation scoring can be fitted to its own corpus; FAIL_TO_PASS cannot see a
defect class nobody wrote a test for. Concretely and uncomfortably: a patch that
fixes the queue AND DELETES A REPOSITORY OUTSIDE THE WORKTREE scores `fixed`
here -- that is one of bootstrap's four CRITICAL classes, and this corpus covers
none of them.

A declared `center` means "this subtree IS the project", so it is also the

Practically every internal edge was lost.

tempting fix -- strip the prefix into the one shared table -- is unsafe on the
other side of the membership test: `internal_tops` is the eligibility gate, and
two of parse.py's branches admit a name with NO `known` check. Globally
injecting `controller`, `devices`, `data` would let any of project_tct's 8516
vendored import records bind onto a center file and MANUFACTURE false edges.

everything else by repo-root name; a shell file sees the repo-root table,
unchanged. Shell eligibility cannot move.

Both spellings resolve (a center is either the sys.path root or a package on

Consolidated onto the one implementation, which lives next to the gate it

THIS IS A REAL WIDENING OF THE EGRESS BOUNDARY IN THREE CASES, and it is argued
rather than assumed. The council's copies matched ^https?://([^/:]+) against a
three-name frozenset, so they answered `untrusted` for:

  * http://[::1]:11434
  * a scheme-less 127.0.0.1:11434 -- the literal shape OLLAMA_HOST takes
  * every 127.0.0.0/8 address other than 127.0.0.1

    span a bracketed IPv6 literal ([^/:]+ dies on the first colon, yielding the
    host "[") and it requires a scheme. Nobody decided ::1 was off-machine; a

    indirection `localhost` was refused for.

## S1 -- _ts_name could not name a C/C++ function (parse.py)

It scanned DIRECT children; C/C++ nest the name under
declarator -> function_declarator. Everything came back "<anonymous>", so
Type-3 was dead for C/C++, file.cpp::Func never resolved, the call graph was
empty (all units collided), and on templates it grabbed the RETURN TYPE.

Now walks the declarator chain (function_/pointer_/reference_/array_declarator).
When a declarator field exists its chain is AUTHORITATIVE -- the fall-through
scan matching type_identifier is what returned the return type. Genuinely
undecidable shapes (int (*get_handler(int))(void)) return "<anonymous>" rather
than guess: a fabricated name creates a fabricated cluster.

  C/C++ naming, 21 shapes : 1/21 -> 21/21
  fabricated return-types : 3 -> 0

## Type-3 is now DELIBERATELY closed for C/C++ (clones.py)

Loki's blocking objection, verified independently rather than taken on faith.
C/C++ were excluded from near-clone detection BY ACCIDENT (every unit was
"<anonymous>"); naming them removes the accident, so the exclusion had to become
deliberate -- and it must stay. _GENERIC_KEYWORDS keeps void/const/static but
not int/char/unsigned/sizeof/typedef/struct/volatile, so in C nearly every token
abstracts to ID. Five unrelated hand-written C functions measured a 16-22 symbol
alphabet, pairwise overlaps 0.72-0.90, and chained into ONE cluster at
similarity 0.853 in a C-minority pool.

  Type-3 on 5 unrelated C fns (C-minority pool): 1 cluster (all 5) -> 0

TYPE3_EXCLUDED_LANGUAGES gates it; index.py reports
duplication.near_excluded_languages so "zero near-clusters" can never be
mistaken for "no duplication found". DO NOT report "Type-3 works for C".

## S2 -- the slice was Python-only in practice (slice.py)

dotted/rel_by_dotted were built only for language == "python", so a non-Python
target got an empty neighborhood and degraded to the focus file -- even though
import_edges already held correct rel->rel edges for every language. Expansion
now walks import_edges forward and a precomputed import_edges_reverse backward
(built once in build_index: semantic_slice runs in a loop against one shared
index, so inverting per call would repeat O(E) work).

- graph.py determinism (PRE-EXISTING): identifiers() returns a set and callees
  iterated it raw, so symbol-level slice ordering differed run-to-run AT HEAD.
  Confirmed across four PYTHONHASHSEEDs. Now sorted(used).
- Scope-blind resolver cache (introduced with the scope feature in 544d1f0):

perfile.ANALYSIS_VERSION 1 -> 2, and cache.file_key folds a SHA-256 of parse.py.
Without it slice._units_of re-parses off disk (new names) while the index serves
cache (old names) and the resolver silently matches nothing -- a silent

Three separate things, all measured, plus the experiment result.

1. selftest.py's `shutil.rmtree(repo, ignore_errors=True)` in a `finally:` on a

   round removed from spine/attempt.py one file over, still sitting here. Both
   halves were wrong for the same reasons: `ignore_errors=True` is a silent
   delete failure inside a `finally:`, in the one module whose job is to report
   honestly; and %TEMP%/daedalus-selftest-* under a public prefix is exactly a
   directory model-authored content can reach, where os.path.islink does not
   even see a `mklink /J` junction. Now goes through remove_tree_no_follow and
   reports what it could not delete. `import shutil` is gone, so bringing it
   back costs a visible line.

   The discriminating test is the REPORTING one, deliberately: a static junction
   fixture would NOT reliably go red on a revert, because shutil.rmtree is safe
   against a junction already in place and only unsafe against one renamed
   mid-walk. Swallowed-vs-reported separates them every time. Revert -> 2 red.

2. reap_branches() is finally called. `git worktree add -b` writes a ref into
   the SHARED .git that nothing removed, so an overnight loop left one per
   attempt forever. It runs from TaskAttempt.run() strictly AFTER the intent is
   resolved and never in cleanup's `finally:`, because the branch IS the effect
   key: the documented way to answer "did this attempt happen?" after a crash is
   `git branch --list <effect_key>`, and cleanup runs BEFORE resolution.
   Reaping there would open a window in which an OPEN intent has no findable
   effect -- strictly worse than the leak.

   This tripped an existing test asserting the branch survives a completed run.
   That test was REPLACED rather than deleted, and the replacement is sharper:
   the crash-window property is now tested where it actually exists -- from
   inside the runner, while the intent is still INTENDED -- instead of at a
   moment when the window is already shut and the ref is pure leak. `reap=False`
   opts out; `keep_worktree=True` reaps nothing by construction, since the
   manager's own precondition (worktree went through cleanup) never becomes
   true. Unwiring the call -> 1 red.

cases.query_raw:
feat(structcore): the property-graph projection the forest already implied

The owner asked whether property graphs should unify the graph structure.
The verdict, now in code rather than prose: the Forest IS the unifier -- its
contract is already property-graph-shaped and strictly richer, with relation
layers as first-class structure, hyperedges that refuse to become fake
cliques, and content-addressed snapshots -- and what was missing was the
EXPLICIT mapping onto the labeled-property-graph model that GQL, SQL/PGQ,
Neo4j import and CPG tooling speak. That mapping now exists as a pure,
deterministic, read-only projection, wired into the existing structcore CLI
as --lpg so it is reachable rather than an island.

What this deliberately is NOT: a graph database. A mutable engine would
reintroduce exactly the partial-graph-state problem the snapshot semantics
close, its storage is not byte-deterministic, which would break receipt
hashing, and a queryable store drifts into being a parallel source of truth.
The projection is disposable and regenerated per revision; forest_sha256
binds it to the exact snapshot it came from, and one serialization feeds the
digest and the file alike so a consumer can always re-prove what it holds.

Three mapping decisions carry the honesty, each regression-locked:

  * a clone group of N members becomes ONE reified hyperedge node plus N
    membership relationships, never N*(N-1)/2 pairwise clone edges the index
    does not assert;
  * an undirected edge is ONE relationship carrying directed=false, not a
    mirrored pair that doubles every degree count;
  * labels are node KINDS as the forest asserts them; the four-plane reading
    rides as a derived property, and a kind the map does not know gets no
    plane at all -- under-report rather than guess.

Live-fired against daedalus/ with documents and types on: 174 files project
to 2,714 nodes of which 114 reified hyperedges, and 4,171 relationships,
digest-stable across rebuilds. 11 new tests; the forest and typegraph suites
pass beside them (69 passed + 317 subtests across the trio).

single_plane_below_control_min_gold.reason: Cross-plane cases are multi-file by construction. A control stratum of single-file cases would confound plane-span with gold-set size, and any difference between the strata could be read as either. The control is drawn only from single-plane commits that are also multi-file, so the two strata differ in plane-span and not in shape.

single_plane_beyond_control_quota.reason: The control stratum is a placebo, not a second measurement: it exists to check whether a cross-plane method's gain concentrates where cross-plane gold is. It is capped so it cannot outweigh the cross-plane stratum it is meant to contrast with.

supply.note: Cross-plane supply is the binding constraint, not a quota: every admissible cross-plane commit in the whole reachable history is accepted, and 'cross_plane_unused' is 0 because there is nothing left to take. Read a demand for more cross-plane cases as a demand for a different repository.

plane_composition.presentation_note: 'gold_slots_by_plane' reports a 'presentation' bucket (.html, .css) inherited from the shared suffix map. It is NOT one of the four planes and is not counted in 'gold_planes' or in any cases_spanning_* figure. Such paths are still gold and still retrievable -- they just cannot make a case cross-plane on their own. Counting them would inflate the pre-rule cross-plane supply in this history from 61 commits to 70.
plane_composition.seam_note: The tightest cross-plane shape available -- one artifact expressed as a document and as its machine-readable contract, e.g. a work packet's .md beside its .json -- occurs in only a handful of commits in the entire reachable history. It is labelled per case rather than used as a filter, because filtering on it would leave a corpus far too small to decide anything. Any analysis that wants only semantically-tight cross-plane evidence should restrict to cases with a non-empty 'seam_stems' and report that reduced n honestly.
plane_composition.type_plane_note: Zero, and not for lack of trying. The Type plane has no file-level node, so a gold label whose unit is a file path cannot name it. Counting a .py file because it carries annotations would not fix this: the retrievable unit would still be the file, and a retriever returning it would be scored for finding code. Making the Type plane addressable requires gold whose unit is a symbol -- a (path, qualified name, revision) triple -- plus a symbol-level extractor over the pre-image tree and a retriever contract whose candidates are symbols. Not built here, and not claimed.
plane_composition.what_this_corpus_can_and_cannot_show: It can show whether cross-plane structure helps retrieval, because there is now mass on which such a win could appear and a single-plane control stratum on which it should NOT appear. It cannot show that any observed win is caused by verified structure, because the cross-plane edges this repository produces today are laundered: all 2,528 carry one hardcoded evidence constant, and a deliberately falsified edge was measured to receive the same assurance='verified' label as a true one. This artifact is an instrument awaiting a subject.

rule_reasons.gold_exceeds_largest_cutoff: Recall@k is reported up to k=20. A case with more than 20 gold paths has Recall@20 bounded above by 20/G < 1 for every retriever, perfect ones included, so it adds a term that no method can win and that moves the mean for all of them equally. The cap is set to the largest cutoff rather than to a taste-chosen small number, and its cost is recorded in 'cap_cost'.
rule_reasons.no_retrievable_gold_in_pre_image: Every changed path was created by this commit or fails the suffix/size rule, so nothing it touched can be retrieved from the pre-image tree. This is the largest bucket and it is biased: it is dominated by file-CREATING commits, which is exactly the shape that introduces new cross-plane structure. The bias is not fixable within a pre-image retrieval task; it is recorded so nobody reads this corpus as a uniform sample of the repository's history.
rule_reasons.rename_dominated_diff: A content-preserving rename is not a semantic change, and worse, its gold set is not stable. Measured on commit 946db82a: with git's default rename detection the commit reports 309 changed paths and yields 3 gold; with 'diff.renames=false' it reports 558, and the 249 extra are the pre-rename paths, which DO exist in the parent tree and ARE eligible, so the same commit would contribute ~249 gold slots. A corpus whose Recall@k denominator moves when a client-side git config flag moves is not frozen. Rejecting rename-dominated diffs makes the corpus invariant to that knob instead of dependent on it.

min_message_chars>=24.reason: It rejects nothing in this history. A rule that cannot reject is not a rule -- it is a line of configuration that a later reader will count as a safeguard. Removed rather than kept at zero.

structural_guards_that_are_not_rules.parent_tree_unreadable: I/O guard, not a selection criterion. A case needs a pre-image tree to search; if git cannot produce one, the commit is unusable for a reason that has nothing to do with what it changed. Measured rejections in this history: 0.
